requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, the CPH number question applies to every live-animal commodity except horses (0101) and commodity code 01061900 (cats, dogs, ferrets and other live mammals). The rule is built now over the commodities today's catalogue holds, and the same rule covers pigs, sheep, goats, poultry, rabbits, camels, ostriches, parrots, reptiles, bees and fish once the MDM catalogue holds them, with no further change. Where it does not apply, the CPH page cannot be opened and sends the user to the consignment addresses page. The plants frontend has no CPH number and gets nothing from this rule.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for a CPH number for every species kept on a holding, not only the few on today's list, and keeps the page out of reach for consignments that have no holding. This is the live half of the CPH rule: the 2026-10-09 ruling splits req-699 per set, and the germinal set has no CPH page at all (req-1832). The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling blocks the new catalogue on MDM but lets the CPH page go ahead on today's five commodities, and never mirrors CPH into plants.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the CPH question applies only when a commodity line's commodity is on the frontend's CPH commodity list (repo-frontend-p10-003): cattle bring it in and cats leave it out (trace-e2e-p6-068, trace-e2e-p6-070), but nothing shows pigs, sheep, goats, poultry and the rest on it, and no source shows what the page does when opened for a consignment it does not apply to. The germinal codes 05111000 and 05119985 leave the live-animals catalogue (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-026), so the live rule no longer names them.

requirements.statement: On the consignment addresses page the CPH section is headed 'County parish holding (CPH) number', described 'The county parish holding (CPH) number identifies the holding where the animals will be kept.', sits after the place of destination, and before a number is saved offers the link 'Add a CPH number'.
requirements.why: The link text is Design Release 2.1's; today's bare 'Add' action reads as nothing on its own.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the heading, description and position already match (trace-e2e-p6-071, trace-e2e-p6-072); the empty row's action is an 'Add' link with the hidden suffix ' county parish holding (cph) number' (trace-e2e-p6-073) instead of the link text 'Add a CPH number'.

requirements.statement: A saved CPH number is shown on the consignment addresses page and on the review page as county/parish/holding with slashes, such as '12/345/6789', with a 'Change' link back to the CPH page.
requirements.why: The slashed form is how traders read and check a CPH number, and it is how Design Release 2.1 shows it everywhere.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the addresses page shows the saved number as nine bare digits, '123456789' (trace-e2e-p6-075); the Change link already exists (trace-e2e-p6-076).

requirements.statement: A valid CPH number is stored as nine bare digits, the three parts joined with no separators, and is split back 2/3/4 into its boxes when the page is shown again.
requirements.why: The stored shape is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express: today's record, and every stored notification, holds nine digits, so only the display gains slashes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-038 and trace-animals-fit-p13-025: the frontend joins the parts and stores 123456789.

requirements.statement: The CPH page has the caption 'Consignment parties', the single h1 'Add the county parish holding number (CPH)', and the browser title 'Add the county parish holding number (CPH) - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the page's identity.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p13-002, trace-animals-fit-p13-003 and trace-animals-fit-p13-004 show the same heading, caption and title today.

requirements.statement: The CPH, permanent address and contact address pages show the notification's 'Draft' tag and reference above the content.
requirements.why: The trader always sees which notification they are changing.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p13-023 and trace-e2e-p7-008: the journey strip with the Draft tag and reference is on the CPH and contact pages today; the permanent address page gets it when it is built.

requirements.statement: A collapsed 'What is a CPH number?' details component sits above the CPH inputs and, when opened, says 'A county parish holding (CPH) number is a unique 9-digit number used to identify land and buildings where livestock are kept, moved or handled.'
requirements.why: Traders who do not know their CPH number need to know what it is before they look for it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-007, repo-frontend-p10-008 and trace-animals-fit-p13-017 show the same summary and definition today.

requirements.statement: The CPH help's second paragraph reads 'You can find your CPH number on documents from the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) or by checking your holding details on GOV.UK.', in English and Welsh, with 'checking your holding details on GOV.UK' as a link to the GOV.UK 'Get a county parish holding (CPH) number' guidance (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/get-a-county-parish-holding-cph-number).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds a second place to find the number and the prototype wins; its href is only a placeholder, so the link opens the GOV.UK page its text names (c-117).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the paragraph ends after '(APHA).' with no GOV.UK clause or link (repo-frontend-p10-009, trace-animals-fit-p13-018).

requirements.statement: The CPH number is asked as one fieldset with the small legend 'CPH number', not as a heading.
requirements.why: One question, one legend, so the page keeps a single h1.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-011 and trace-animals-fit-p13-006: a role=group fieldset with the small legend 'CPH number' today.

requirements.statement: The CPH question's hint reads 'For example 12/345/6789', with no comma and no full stop, and describes the whole group.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's wording of the hint.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the hint reads 'For example, 12/345/6789.', with a comma and a full stop (repo-frontend-p10-012, trace-animals-fit-p13-007); it already describes the group and never shows 123/456/789.

requirements.statement: The CPH number is entered in three boxes in one row, laid out with the GOV.UK date-input pattern, with visible labels 'County' (2 wide, at most 2 characters), 'Parish' (3 wide, at most 3) and 'Holding number' (4 wide, at most 4), each asking for a numeric keypad.
requirements.why: A CPH number is three parts of 2, 3 and 4 digits; boxes sized to the parts make each part easy to enter and check.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-014 to repo-frontend-p10-020 and trace-animals-fit-p13-010 to trace-animals-fit-p13-015: the same three labelled, sized boxes in the date-input layout today.

requirements.statement: Each CPH box has autocomplete turned off and the pattern [0-9]* as well as the numeric input mode.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sets both so browsers do not offer unrelated saved values and phones show the digit keypad.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each box has inputmode numeric and spellcheck off, but no autocomplete=off and no pattern (repo-frontend-p10-017, trace-animals-fit-p13-014).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, each CPH box drops any non-digit as the trader types and stops at its maximum length.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps stray characters out of the boxes as they are typed. The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling (design question 7) builds nothing new on the CPH page now: it already works without JavaScript, with the server's checks (req-715), so this script is its own waiting-on-design increment, built as design answers or dropped. The automatic focus moves the same prototype script makes are not built (c-006, req-713).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the boxes are plain text inputs with no script (trace-animals-fit-p13-014 shows the attributes only), and non-digits are caught only on save.
requirements.blockedBy: Design answers design question 7 (CPH number JavaScript) in the waiting-on-design theme: whether the CPH boxes drop non-digits as they are typed. Built as design says, or dropped if design drops it.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, pasting into a CPH box keeps only the digits and spreads them across that box and the ones after it (2, 3 then 4 digits), so pasting 123456789 or 12/345/6789 into County fills all three boxes.
requirements.why: Traders often copy the whole number from an APHA document; Design Release 2.1 lets one paste fill the three parts. The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling (design question 7) moves this script to the waiting-on-design theme, together with the question of whether one box that takes '12/345/6789' should replace the three; the page works as today until design answers.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a whole slashed number pasted into County stays there and is rejected on save with 'County must be 2 digits' and the missing-part errors (repo-frontend-p10-033); without JavaScript that stays the case.
requirements.blockedBy: Design answers design question 7 (CPH number JavaScript) in the waiting-on-design theme: whether a paste spreads across the three CPH boxes, and whether one box taking '12/345/6789' replaces the three. Built as design says, or dropped if design drops it.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, focus moves to the next CPH box once a box is full, and Backspace in an empty box moves focus back to the previous box and deletes its last digit.
requirements.why: Moving focus while the trader types is a change of context that accessibility guidance warns against, and the accessibility duty overrides Design Release 2.1 here: the automatic focus moves are not built (c-006). The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling adds that the prototype's JavaScript is not copied into the frontend; the digit filtering and paste spreading wait on design (req-711, req-712).
requirements.deltaNote: Today nothing moves focus between the boxes.

requirements.statement: Saving the CPH page with all three boxes empty raises no error: it saves no CPH number (clearing any saved before), the trader moves on, and the CPH section stays incomplete, so the notification cannot be submitted until a number is added.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader move on and holds the gap at submission instead; required-to-proceed is a design choice the prototype can express, not a constraint it cannot.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an empty submit is refused with 400 and the single error 'Enter a CPH number' linked to the County box.

requirements.statement: A partly filled or wrongly formed CPH number is refused with one error per wrong part, in county, parish, holding order: 'Enter the county', 'Enter the parish' or 'Enter the holding number' for a missing part; 'County must be 2 digits', 'Parish must be 3 digits' or 'Holding number must be 4 digits' for a wrong length; 'County must only contain numbers', 'Parish must only contain numbers' or 'Holding number must only contain numbers' for a non-digit. Parts are trimmed first, and a whole slashed number typed into one box is refused.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express: Design Release 2.1 silently drops a part-entered number, which loses what the trader typed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-023 to repo-frontend-p10-033 and trace-animals-fit-p13-035 to trace-animals-fit-p13-041: these per-part messages are the frontend's today.

requirements.statement: CPH errors re-render the page with status 400 and every typed value kept: an error summary titled 'There is a problem' links each error to its box and moves focus there, one inline message on the whole question lists every error (with a hidden 'Error:' prefix, between the hint and the boxes), each wrong box gets the error border, and the group's description includes the error.
requirements.why: A three-part question needs one message on the question and a border on each wrong part, so the trader sees which part to fix.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-034 to repo-frontend-p10-037 and trace-animals-fit-p13-042: the error presentation is the frontend's today.

requirements.statement: A stored CPH number that is not nine digits is flagged on the page with 'The saved CPH number is no longer valid. Re-enter the county, parish and holding numbers.', linked to the County box, with all three boxes shown empty.
requirements.why: Stored data can predate today's rules; the trader is told to re-enter it rather than shown stray digits.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-041 and repo-frontend-p10-042.

requirements.statement: The CPH page opens with three empty boxes when nothing is saved, and with the saved parts filled back in (County 12, Parish 345, Holding number 6789) when a number is saved, however the page is reached.
requirements.why: The trader can check and change what they entered.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-039, repo-frontend-p10-040 and trace-e2e-p6-077.

requirements.statement: The CPH page's back link always goes to the consignment addresses page.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the CPH page is a step of the consignment addresses section, opened from it and returning to it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the back link goes to the addresses page only when reached with return=addresses (repo-frontend-p10-043, trace-e2e-p6-078); reached any other way it goes to the notification overview.

requirements.statement: 'Save and continue' on the CPH page always returns to the consignment addresses page, never on to the contact address page or the notification overview.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns every consignment-addresses step to the addresses page, from where 'Save and continue' moves on.
requirements.deltaNote: Today saving returns to the addresses page only when reached with return=addresses (trace-e2e-p6-074); in the opening run it continues to the contact page, and otherwise it goes to the notification overview.

requirements.statement: The CPH page ends with the primary 'Save and continue' button alone, with no return-to-hub button and no cancel link.
requirements.why: DR1's inc-161 judgement (rule b): only pages the task-list overview links to end with the three return controls, and the CPH page is reached from the consignment addresses page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-047, trace-animals-fit-p13-020 and trace-e2e-p6-089: the CPH page ends with 'Save and continue' alone today.

requirements.statement: In the journey's first pass, 'Save and continue' on the consignment addresses page goes on to the contact address page, whether or not the CPH number applies; opened from its overview task, the consignment addresses page returns to the overview instead (req-1615). The CPH page is reached only from its own link on the addresses page, never as the next step after it.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the contact address follows the consignment addresses, and the CPH number is one of the addresses page's sections, not a step after it. The 2026-10-09 ruling has a page opened from its overview task return to the overview, and removes the rule that Roles and addresses opened from the overview runs on to the CPH page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the addresses page's 'Save and continue' goes to the CPH page when a CPH-triggering line exists, and otherwise to the notification overview, without requiring any party.

requirements.statement: The CPH and contact address forms, and the plants consignment contact form, post back to their own URL with a CSRF crumb and the notification's concurrency token, and a failed save re-renders the page with status 500, the recoverable-error banner and the trader's values kept. On the plants contact page an unavailable address book raises the error rather than treating the contact as deleted or unselected.
requirements.why: Real persistence and concurrency constraints the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p13-024, repo-frontend-p10-048 and repo-frontend-p10-078; for plants, repo-plantsfrontend-p7-102, repo-plantsfrontend-p7-081 and repo-plantsfrontend-p7-082.

requirements.statement: The CPH, permanent address and contact address pages, and the plants consignment contact page, have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A/AA axe violations, clean and in their error states, and each radio group's description names its hint and, on error, its error.
requirements.why: The service must be accessible; the prototype does not test this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-049 and repo-frontend-p10-082 for the CPH and contact pages today, and repo-plantsfrontend-p7-084 for the plants contact page; the permanent address page needs the same check when it is built.

requirements.statement: Every English string changed or added on the CPH, permanent address and contact address pages, and on the plants consignment contact page, gets a Welsh version in the same change, marked as a machine draft that must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: These pages already carry a Welsh version of every string, so a changed English string without its Welsh would leave the Welsh page wrong.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the CPH and contact pages, and the plants contact page ('Cyfeiriad cyswllt ar gyfer y llwyth', repo-plantsfrontend-p7-085), have machine-draft Welsh for today's strings (repo-frontend-p10-051, repo-frontend-p10-084); the new and changed strings have none yet.

requirements.statement: Cats, dogs and ferrets need a permanent address; 'Other live mammals', which shares their commodity code 01061900, does not. It is built now for cats and dogs, and the same rule takes in ferrets once the commodity catalogue holds them.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for a permanent address only for pets that APHA must be able to check. The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling builds the permanent address page for cats and dogs now, and ferrets once the catalogue, which waits on MDM, holds them.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the frontend asks for a permanent address for cats and dogs only (trace-e2e-p6-028; DR1 inc-057 records the same); ferrets are not in today's commodity catalogue, so nothing changes for them until the MDM catalogue holds them.

requirements.statement: The permanent address is its own page in the consignment parties section, opened from the consignment addresses page, at a slug of its own in the live-animals set's addresses section (not the prototype's /permanent-address/select path): caption 'Consignment parties', heading 'Permanent address', browser title 'Permanent address - Import notification service - GOV.UK', and a back link to the consignment addresses page. It applies only when the consignment holds commodity 01061900 with at least one species that needs a permanent address; otherwise the page cannot be opened and sends the user to the consignment addresses page. The address fields leave the animal identification form.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 (and DR1 before it) asks for the permanent address as its own step, so a trader can answer it, leave it and come back, instead of reopening animal identification. The 2026-10-09 ruling gives the new page a real slug in the addresses section, because the prototype never decides URL paths.
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no permanent address page: the address fields sit inside the animal identification form after the identifier fields (trace-e2e-p6-028, document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-058).

requirements.statement: When the permanent address applies, the consignment addresses page has a 'Permanent address' section explaining 'A permanent address is where an animal:' with the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', and the link 'Add a permanent address' to the permanent address page; for cats it has no CPH section.
requirements.why: The section is how the trader reaches the permanent address step in Design Release 2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the addresses page has no permanent address section (trace-e2e-p6-068 lists its rows for cats).

requirements.statement: Once permanent addresses are saved, the consignment addresses page shows the one address with a 'Change' link when every animal is 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' or only one animal has an address; otherwise it shows 'Permanent addresses added for N animals', where N is the number of animals that need one, with a 'Change' link. The Change link goes straight to the permanent address page.
requirements.why: The trader sees at a glance what was given for the section, without one row per animal.

requirements.statement: The permanent address shows the GOV.UK warning 'Providing a false address is an act of fraud', with no full stop.
requirements.why: Traders must know a false address is fraud before they give one.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p6-029: the identification form's permanent address block shows the same warning, with no full stop, today; it moves with the fields to the new page.

requirements.statement: The permanent address explains 'A permanent address is where an animal:' followed by the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', then asks 'Where will their permanent address be?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the explanation and the question.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p6-030 and trace-e2e-p6-031: the same copy on the identification form today (the question an h3 there, an h2 on the new page).

requirements.statement: The permanent address page shows one card for each animal that needs a permanent address, as many as the number of animals entered for that species, each headed with the species' scientific name and a running number, such as 'Felis catus 1'; species that do not need one get no cards.
requirements.why: Each animal can live at a different address, and the page asks for all of them in one place.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address is asked once per animal record inside the identification form, which opens one animal at a time ('Enter details for Felis catus 2 of 2', trace-e2e-p6-044).

requirements.statement: Each animal card shows, in inset text, the identifiers already entered for that animal as 'label: value' (such as 'Microchip: MICROCHIP-1'), leaving out blank ones, and no inset when none are entered.
requirements.why: The trader can tell which animal each card is for.

requirements.statement: Each animal card has a radio group with the legend 'Select an address' and two options, 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' and 'Enter a new address', with neither chosen when the page first opens.
requirements.why: Most pets live at the place of destination; reusing it saves the trader typing the same address again.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address fields are always shown, with no choice to reuse an address already given (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-004).

requirements.statement: Once a place of destination is given, the 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' option shows that address on one line as its hint, such as 'Riverside Holding Facility, East Farm Road, Leeds, LS25 3EB, United Kingdom'.
requirements.why: The trader sees which address they are reusing.

requirements.statement: The 'Enter a new address' option has the hint 'This is where they will stay after spending 48 hours at the place of destination.'
requirements.why: It tells the trader what the permanent address means for a pet that moves on from the place of destination.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the frontend carries the 48-hour hint nowhere (document-dr1-parity-backlog-p6-006-m1).

requirements.statement: Choosing 'Enter a new address' reveals that animal's own address fields inside its card, as a GOV.UK conditional reveal.
requirements.why: The fields are only needed when the place of destination is not reused.

requirements.statement: A new permanent address asks for 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', 'County (optional)', 'Postcode or Zip code', 'Email address' and 'Phone number' (hint 'For international numbers include the country code'), and has no country field.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today ask for the same fields.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p6-032 to trace-e2e-p6-035: the identification form asks for the same eight fields with the same labels and phone hint, and no country, today.

requirements.statement: In a new permanent address, 'Email address' comes before 'Phone number'.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's field order.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Phone number' comes before 'Email address' (trace-e2e-p6-032).

requirements.statement: When 'Enter a new address' is chosen for an animal, its name, address line 1, town or city, postcode, email address and phone number are required, showing 'Enter a name or organisation name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Enter an email address' and 'Enter a phone number' on the blank fields; address line 2 and county are optional; and email, phone and postcode are only checked for being blank.
requirements.why: The choice decides whether an address is needed, so the fields are required exactly when the trader says they will enter one.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the same field messages exist, but they fire whenever any part of the address is given, with no choice behind them (trace-e2e-p6-036 to trace-e2e-p6-042); no source shows today's message for a blank name.

requirements.statement: On the permanent address page, each address error in the error summary names its animal, such as 'Enter a name or organisation name for Felis catus 1' and 'Enter address line 1 for Felis catus 1', and links to the field; the inline message on the field leaves the animal out.
requirements.why: With several animals' forms on one page, the summary must say which animal each error is about.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the error summary repeats the field message without naming the animal ('Enter address line 1', trace-e2e-p6-037), since one animal's form is shown at a time.

requirements.statement: Choosing 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' for an animal before a place of destination is given shows 'Add a place of destination before you can continue' on that animal's radios and in an error summary titled 'There is a problem', linked to the radios.
requirements.why: There is nothing to reuse until the place of destination exists.

requirements.statement: An animal left with no option chosen raises no error: the page saves the other animals and moves on, and the permanent address section stays incomplete until every animal that needs one has an address with a name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader save what they know and come back; completeness is checked at the section and at submission.

requirements.statement: When the permanent address page shows errors, each animal's chosen option stays selected and a chosen 'Enter a new address' keeps its fields open with what was typed; when the page is opened again, each animal's saved choice is selected and its saved address filled back in.
requirements.why: The trader never has to re-enter what they already gave.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the identification form keeps typed values on a failed add (trace-e2e-p6-043); the new page needs the same per animal.

requirements.statement: When no animals that need a permanent address have been counted, the permanent address page shows 'Add the number of animals on consignment details before you can continue.', with 'consignment details' linking to that page, instead of the animal cards; saving from that state saves nothing and returns to the consignment addresses page.
requirements.why: The cards depend on the number of animals, which is given on the consignment details page.

requirements.statement: Saving 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' for an animal gives that animal the place of destination's address as its permanent address (name, address lines, country, email and phone, as the review then shows); saving 'Enter a new address' gives it the animal's own name, address lines, town or city, county, postcode, country United Kingdom, email and phone. Whether the same-as-destination answer is held as a copy of the place of destination or as a reference to it, and where the answer is stored, is for the plan to decide in the real service's model.
requirements.why: Each animal's permanent address must be held with the notification, whichever way it was given. The 2026-10-09 ruling keeps this behaviour but leaves its storage shape to the plan, because the prototype never decides the data model (c-239).
requirements.deltaNote: Today each animal record stores the address typed on the identification form; nothing gives an animal the place of destination's address.

requirements.statement: A new permanent address keeps every field in its own place: the county is saved, and a saved address with no address line 2 opens with the town in 'Town or city' and the postcode in 'Postcode or Zip code'.
requirements.why: Persistence is a real constraint the prototype cannot express: Design Release 2.1 loses the county and shifts fields on return, which the real service must not copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's identification form stores each field by name (trace-e2e-p6-032); the new page must keep that.

requirements.statement: The permanent address page ends with the primary 'Save and continue' button alone, which saves and returns to the consignment addresses page.
requirements.why: DR1's inc-161 judgement (rule b): a page reached from another page, not from the task-list overview, ends with the primary button alone, like the CPH page and the party pickers.

requirements.statement: The review page shows the permanent address as one row per animal, labelled with the species' common name and number (such as 'Domestic dog 1'), whose value is that animal's saved address; with no animals counted it shows a single row 'Address'.
requirements.why: The trader checks each animal's permanent address before submitting.
requirements.deltaNote: No today source shows the permanent address on the review page.

requirements.statement: The prototype's own permanent-address routing is not reproduced: /permanent-address resetting the answer and redirecting to /permanent-address/select, the unused 'Are all the animals going to the place of destination?' page, and the retired /permanent-address/enter-address redirect.
requirements.why: These are prototype internals with no behaviour a trader sees beyond landing on the per-animal page; the real service has none of these routes to retire.

requirements.statement: The prototype's custom heading, card and layout classes on the contact and permanent address pages, and its /design-release-2.1 mount paths, are not reproduced.
requirements.why: They are how the prototype is built, not behaviour a trader sees; the real pages use GOV.UK Frontend components.

requirements.statement: The contact address page, in the animals sets and in plants, has the h1 'Contact address for consignment', no section caption, and the browser title 'Contact address for consignment - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the page's identity, and the plants contact page already shares it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-058 and trace-animals-fit-p12-041: the same heading and title, with no caption, today (as the radios legend); repo-plantsfrontend-p7-048 and repo-plantsfrontend-p7-050 for plants.

requirements.statement: Directly under the contact page's heading, body text reads 'This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks.', replacing the hint 'Selecting a contact copies their name and address into this notification.' The plants consignment contact page takes the same change in the same increment, in English and Welsh.
requirements.why: It tells the trader whose address this is; DR1 inc-046 judged the copy sentence loses nothing the trader can act on. The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling has plants' contact picker take the new intro in the same increment, because plants has the same page with the same hint.

positions.says: Blank boxes save no CPH number and the user moves on without an error.
All three boxes empty shows 'Enter a CPH number'.
The CPH number is required: the page cannot be saved without one.
An empty submit shows 'Enter a CPH number' linked to County.
The CPH page refuses an empty submit with an error summary.
Submitting with all three boxes empty shows the single error 'Enter a CPH number'.
The 'Enter a CPH number' error links to and focuses the County box.
When the whole number is missing, only the County box is styled as in error.

In the empty-CPH error state the error summary sits between the journey strip and the caption.

The back link goes to the roles and addresses page.

Outside the opening run and without return context, saving goes to the hub.

Reached sequentially, saving returns to the notification overview.
Reached sequentially, the back link goes to the notification overview.
